answer: Each agent joins the economy only after its host enclave sends a remote attestation bound to a hardware fuse key unique to that processor, and the registry stores a one-way hash of that key as the identity kernel; any duplicate hash is rejected. Because a fake agent must own a separate TEE-equipped chip and pass the same attestation, a sybil voyage across the network becomes expensive linearly in silicon and power, not just cheap cloud accounts. To keep the registry from drifting into a soft nebula of claims, attestations expire and require periodic re-quoting.
